title: VPN & Proxy Security Checklist: Complete Privacy Guide
metaDescription: Essential VPN and proxy security checklist to protect your privacy online. Verify logging policies, test for leaks, and secure your connection.
intro: Protect your online privacy with this comprehensive VPN and proxy security checklist. Learn to verify no-log policies, test for DNS leaks, configure kill switches, and ensure your connection is truly secure from ISP tracking and surveillance.

items.task: Verify the VPN's no-log policy and independent audits
items.why: Many VPNs claim not to log but haven't been independently verified. Real no-log policies are crucial for privacy protection.
items.howTo: Check for third-party security audits, court cases proving no-log claims, and transparency reports. Look for providers audited by firms like Cure53 or Deloitte.

items.task: Research the VPN provider's legal jurisdiction
items.why: VPNs based in 5/9/14 Eyes countries may be compelled to share data with intelligence agencies.
items.howTo: Verify the company's incorporation location. Prefer jurisdictions like Switzerland, Panama, or the British Virgin Islands with strong privacy laws.

items.task: Confirm strong encryption protocols are supported
items.why: Weak encryption can be broken by adversaries, compromising your privacy and security.
items.howTo: Look for OpenVPN, WireGuard, or IKEv2 protocols with AES-256 encryption. Avoid PPTP and older protocols that are known to be vulnerable.

items.task: Verify if the VPN owns or rents its servers
items.why: Owned servers provide better security control, while rented servers may have additional privacy risks from third-party access.
items.howTo: Check the provider's website for server ownership information. RAM-only servers that can't store data permanently are ideal.

items.task: Check for anonymous payment methods
items.why: Credit card payments can be linked back to your identity, reducing anonymity benefits.
items.howTo: Look for cryptocurrency payment options, gift cards, or cash payments. Create accounts with anonymous email addresses when possible.

items.task: Run DNS leak tests to ensure queries aren't exposed
items.why: DNS leaks can reveal your browsing activity to your ISP even when using a VPN, defeating the purpose of privacy protection.
items.howTo: Use tools like dnsleaktest.com or ipleak.net while connected to your VPN. Ensure all DNS servers shown belong to your VPN provider, not your ISP.

items.task: Check for WebRTC IP leaks in your browser
items.why: WebRTC can leak your real IP address through browser vulnerabilities, bypassing VPN protection entirely.
items.howTo: Visit browserleaks.com/webrtc while connected to VPN. If you see your real IP, disable WebRTC in browser settings or Use a privacy-focused browser with WebRTC protection.

items.task: Confirm your IP address is masked and changed
items.why: The primary function of VPNs is IP masking. If your real IP is visible, the VPN isn't working properly.
items.howTo: Check your IP at whatismyipaddress.com before and after connecting to VPN. The location and ISP should change completely.

items.task: Test the VPN kill switch functionality
items.why: Without a working kill switch, your traffic could be exposed if the VPN connection drops unexpectedly.
items.howTo: Connect to VPN, start a download, then disconnect VPN manually. Traffic should stop immediately. Reconnect and verify no data leaked during disconnection.

items.task: Verify IPv6 traffic is properly handled
items.why: Many VPNs only protect IPv4 traffic, potentially leaking your IPv6 address and location information.
items.howTo: Visit test-ipv6.com while connected to VPN. Ensure IPv6 is either disabled or routed through the VPN tunnel properly.

items.task: Run speed tests on multiple servers and times
items.why: Consistent speeds indicate reliable infrastructure. Dramatic speed drops may suggest overloaded servers or connection issues.
items.howTo: Use speedtest.net to test speeds on different VPN servers at various times. Document results and compare with baseline speeds without VPN.

items.task: Configure VPN to connect automatically on startup
items.why: Manual connection increases the risk of forgetting to connect, leaving your traffic exposed to ISPs and surveillance.
items.howTo: Enable auto-connect on system startup in your VPN client settings. Set it to connect to your preferred server location automatically.

items.task: Set up split tunneling if needed for specific apps
items.why: Split tunneling allows certain apps to bypass the VPN while keeping others protected, useful for local services or banking apps.
items.howTo: In VPN settings, add apps that need direct internet access to the split tunneling exclusion list. Use sparingly to maintain privacy.

items.task: Keep VPN client software updated to latest version
items.why: Updates often include security patches and protocol improvements that protect against newly discovered vulnerabilities.
items.howTo: Enable automatic updates in VPN client settings or check for updates weekly. Subscribe to provider's security announcements for critical updates.

items.task: Set custom DNS servers for additional privacy
items.why: Using privacy-focused DNS servers adds another layer of protection against tracking and censorship.
items.howTo: Configure DNS settings to use providers like Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), Quad9 (9.9.9.9), or your VPN's DNS servers for consistent protection.

items.task: Verify your apparent location matches VPN server
items.why: Accurate geolocation spoofing is essential for bypassing geo-blocks and maintaining location privacy.
items.howTo: Visit whatismylocation.com or Google 'what is my location' while connected to different VPN servers. Location should match server location.

items.task: Document your VPN configuration and test results
items.why: Keeping records helps identify issues quickly and ensures consistent security settings across devices.
items.howTo: Create a simple document noting your preferred servers, speed test results, and any custom configurations for future reference.

items.task: Confirm proxy service uses HTTPS/SOCKS5 encryption
items.why: HTTP proxies transmit data in plain text, making them vulnerable to interception and man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.howTo: Check proxy configuration for HTTPS or SOCKS5 protocols. Avoid HTTP proxies for sensitive activities. Verify SSL certificate validity.

items.task: Test proxy anonymity level and header forwarding
items.why: Transparent proxies forward your real IP address, while anonymous proxies may still reveal proxy usage through headers.
items.howTo: Use tools like whatismyipaddress.com/proxy-check to verify anonymity level. Elite proxies should show no proxy detection or real IP leakage.

items.task: Research proxy provider's data retention policies
items.why: Unlike VPNs, many proxy services log user activity and may not have clear privacy policies protecting user data.
items.howTo: Review proxy service terms of service and privacy policy. Look for specific statements about data retention and sharing practices.

items.task: Test proxy uptime and connection stability
items.why: Unreliable proxies can cause connection drops that expose your real IP address during sensitive activities.
items.howTo: Monitor proxy connection over several hours. Test connection stability during different activities like streaming or downloading.

items.task: Set up secure authentication for proxy access
items.why: Unsecured proxy connections can be hijacked by malicious actors, potentially exposing your traffic to interception.
items.howTo: Use strong usernames and passwords for proxy authentication. Enable two-factor authentication if available from the proxy provider.

pro_tips: Use a privacy-focused browser with built-in proxy protection and WebRTC leak prevention for maximum privacy during sensitive browsing sessions.
Test your VPN/proxy setup monthly using different leak testing tools, as new vulnerabilities and testing methods are constantly being discovered.
Consider using Tor over VPN for maximum anonymity, but be aware this significantly reduces connection speeds and may trigger security alerts.
Keep a backup VPN service from a different provider and jurisdiction in case your primary service experiences issues or legal challenges.
Avoid free VPN and proxy services for anything important - they often monetize by selling user data or injecting ads, defeating privacy purposes.
